clue.text: Top composer, the last one to come round to milky coffee

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.text: the last one to come round
indicators.note: the final 'one' (the letter I) in the composer's name turns into a 'round' letter, O

parts.note: Giacomo Puccini, the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: Someone claims the best composer is whoever is last to come round for a milky coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last one to come round' reads as a latecomer, but it tells you the last I (one) of PUCCINI becomes O (round), giving PUCCINO after CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an espresso topped with steamed, frothed milk.

clue.text: One penal settlement in the mountains

indicators.note: a settlement here is the letters of the words settling into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A remote prison colony stands high up among the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penal settlement' looks like one phrase for a prison colony, but 'settlement' is the anagram signal working on I (One) plus PENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes anything found in or typical of high mountain country.

clue.text: Hat obscures soldiers' view

indicators.note: the hat covers up the soldiers, so one piece sits hidden inside the other

parts.note: a Panama is a wide-brimmed straw hat
OR, 'other ranks', is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A wide-brimmed hat blocks the troops from seeing the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken outlook over an area.

clue.text: Guard from illness, taking the waters

parts.note: a cold is a common minor illness
a stream is a body of running water

explanation.surface: Someone protects themselves from sickness by taking a cure at a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard from illness' wants to mean protect against disease; 'Guard' is the definition and 'from' a link. The Coldstream Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Coldstream Guards, a regiment of the British Army's Household Division, is called a Coldstream Guard.

clue.text: Enlisted man sent up to excellent base

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word up means writing it from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: a GI is an enlisted soldier in the US Army
noble can mean excellent or of fine quality

explanation.surface: A private soldier is posted to a first-rate military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp, but it is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base, as an adjective, means morally low or contemptible, the same sense as dishonourable.

clue.text: Passover report raised in I Timothy

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means reading them upwards, so the run is reversed
the word sits within the letters of the book's title

explanation.surface: An account of the Jewish festival turns up in a book of the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passover' looks like the Jewish festival, but read as 'pass over' it means leave out. Reading ITIMO upwards gives the answer; 'report' seems only to add to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over something is to leave it out or skip it.

clue.text: Bear is seen at the roadside

definitions.meaning: to bear a burden is to take its weight on your back
the hard strip at the edge of a road where cars can stop

explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a load is to bear it, and the strip along the edge of a motorway is its hard shoulder.

clue.text: Vote made official before miners hold start of debate

parts.note: a ref is a referee, the official in charge of a match
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the miners' union holds a letter inside it

parts.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: the first letter of the word debate

explanation.surface: A ballot is held after an officer speaks first, before the miners' union opens its discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a vote put to the whole electorate on a single question.

clue.text: West, concealing his odd club

indicators.note: the film star's name wraps round and so hides the other letters

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of the word his are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named West is hiding a strange club of his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns HIS into SHI, which 'concealing' puts inside MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie was an old golf club with a lofted iron head, roughly a modern five-iron.

clue.text: Unveil scheme for office interior

parts.note: to unveil something is to open it to view
a scheme is a plan

explanation.surface: A designer reveals the layout for the inside of an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-plan offices have no internal walls, so the whole working space is one large room.

clue.text: Shed you once found in the river

indicators.note: the old word for you is found inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword favourite
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A garden shed someone once had turns up in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is the name of several English rivers; 'the river' in a Times clue often means it.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small building next to a house, like a shed.

clue.text: Platform for doctors to hold start of examination

indicators.note: the doctors' body holds a letter inside it

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body

indicators.note: the first letter of the word examination

explanation.surface: A stage is set up for doctors to begin an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bema is a raised platform for a speaker, as in ancient Athens or a synagogue.

clue.text: Shape forged in white 'eat in France?

parts.note: blanc is French for white
French mange means eats, here given a dropped-h touch

explanation.surface: Something is cast in white in a playful French accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France?' covers both pieces: BLANC is white in French and MANGE is eat. A 'shape' is an old British name for a moulded pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A blancmange is a sweet milk pudding set in a mould, which is why it was once called a shape.

clue.text: Ring the Captain's place — you'll have to pay for your passage here

definitions.text: you'll have to pay for your passage here

parts.note: to toll a bell is to ring it
a ship's captain commands from the bridge

explanation.surface: Ring the ship's captain on the bridge: crossing will cost you.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll bridge charges a fee to everyone who crosses it.

clue.text: New partner free to seek accommodation outside

indicators.note: the word for seek goes outside, around, the word for free

parts.note: to beg is to seek or ask for
to rid is to free
room means space or lodging

explanation.surface: A newly free person goes looking for somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BEG around RID, making BRIDEG, before ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is a man just married or about to marry, so a husband who is newly wed.

clue.text: Embarrassed, being found in the morning in a shack

indicators.note: the morning sits inside the word for shack

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut or shack
a.m. stands for the morning

explanation.surface: Someone is red-faced when discovered one morning in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel ashamed is to feel embarrassed and guilty about something.

clue.text: On the sly? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong as a verb means misused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they acted secretly: not so!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: ON THE SLY rearranged gives the answer, and denying that something was done on the sly is to say it was done truthfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something not in secret but openly and truthfully is to do it with integrity.

clue.text: Reckoned to be ornamental

explanation.definitionFit: To have figured is to have reckoned or calculated, and figured cloth is woven with decorative patterns.

clue.text: Dinner up! — it's prepared to give you strength

indicators.note: a prepared dish is made up from its parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook announces dinner, a meal made to build you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dinner up!' sounds like a call to the table; its letters, 'prepared', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin something is to support it from beneath, to strengthen it.

clue.text: One can grasp this, but barely control it

definitions.meaning: as much as a single hand can hold
a person or animal that is hard to manage

explanation.definitionFit: A handful is the amount held in one hand, and a difficult child or pet is called a handful.

clue.text: Perfect trick brings total victory on board

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a sum is a total
mate is checkmate, the winning move in chess

explanation.surface: A clever ruse wins someone an overall victory at a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' points to chess, where MATE is the winning move.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate means complete or perfect, as consummate skill.

clue.text: The end of Aunt Ada

definitions.meaning: Aunt Ada's surname in Stella Gibbons's novel Cold Comfort Farm

explanation.definitionFit: Doom means final ruin or fate, and Aunt Ada Doom is the matriarch of Cold Comfort Farm, a comic English novel.

clue.text: Nowhere to cook in the house?

parts.note: nothing, written as the letter O
a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: A home has no kitchen at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nowhere' splits into No (O) and where to cook (RANGE). The House of Orange is the Dutch royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty, a house in the sense of a ruling family.

clue.text: Taken up and wrapped, say

definitions.meaning: wrapped up in something, totally engaged by it

explanation.definitionFit: Someone engrossed in a book is taken up with it or wrapped up in it.

clue.text: Part of the country to retire to?

explanation.definitionFit: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county, and you retire to bed at night.

clue.text: Failing, so going for the high jump

definitions.meaning: falling flat or collapsing, as a show does
using the Fosbury flop, the back-first high-jump style

explanation.definitionFit: A play that is flopping is failing, and the Fosbury flop is the standard high-jump technique.

clue.text: Excavate round about meadow, not a balmy place?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, around, the meadow
turned round, so the word for excavate is read backwards

parts.note: to dig is to excavate
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: Dig around a field: hardly a warm spot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns DIG into GID, which goes 'about' LEA. The definition plays on Jeremiah's question asking whether there is no balm in that land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible asks whether there is any balm in this land, so the question mark hints it may have none.

clue.text: Siren fabled to like it hot

definitions.meaning: an eel-like amphibian of North America, of the newt family
a creature said in legend to live in fire

explanation.definitionFit: Sirens are tailed amphibians related to newts, and medieval lore held that this creature could live in flames.
